From a candidate dataset to an Atlas source

Loading the catalog…

The RL Data Atlas lists every RL task source that Marin — the open training project whose job scheduler, dataset processing and app host this Atlas runs on — has declared, with its review state and evidence. A source is one pinned population of tasks, for example one Hugging Face dataset revision. A task is one RL problem stored as a TaskSpec: the prompt, the machine environment the agent works in, the answer contract and the grader (also called the verifier).

This page shows each path a dataset can take into the Atlas and what each outcome lets you rely on. Being listed is not the same as being approved for training: see the eligibility matrix, and the reader workflow for using an existing source. The counts come from the catalog snapshot that the Atlas currently serves, so they change when an operator loads a new snapshot. The normative rules live in the task curation reference; the steps below link to the maintained procedures.

The paths

Solid edges are the path a candidate takes; dashed edges leave it for an outcome or an alternate route. Agentic tasks need a machine (a shell, files or tools). Reply-only tasks skip machine provisioning; every source still needs a grading-boundary assessment. Select an outcome to list its sources.

the candidate's required path exit into an outcome, or an alternate route such as the non-agentic bypass

Read the evidence before selecting data

Quality measures QA coverage: QUICK has no qualifying execution oversight, SAMPLE records executed oversight while content QA can remain incomplete, and FULL requires a complete content-review assembly bound to the exact retained population. Partial content reviews are provisional. Execution qualification is recorded separately: complete content QA does not prove that the tasks execute successfully.

Result is computed from conclusive content reviews: GOOD means at most 10% with issues, BAD means at least 50%, and SOME_ISSUES lies between. Uncertain and unavailable observations stay explicit. QC never rejects tasks or sources. Mechanical conversion, environment, oracle and contamination exclusions have their own ledgers. A missing Result is unassessed, not a clean result.

Some issues · provisional A Result marked provisional uses incomplete content reviews. The Issue rate column shows the conclusive issue fraction; review progress and lower bounds are on the source Evidence page. Enum chips carry their whole label with no text beneath them. The Overlap column counts flagged tasks in the measured input.

Contamination

Contamination records lexical overlap with the evaluation corpus. Counts refer to the measured input population, before duplicate and lexical exclusions. This measurement does not establish semantic decontamination.

NO ISSUES
A lexical measurement exists and reports zero overlapping tasks.
REMEDIATED
TRAIN overlap was found and excluded in a new pinned private TaskCompendium release. Its validated remediation receipt must match the current dataset pin.
MEASURED, EVAL
Overlap was measured for an EVAL or benchmark source and retained by policy. Inspect the overlapping-task count and matched evaluations in Evidence.
REMEDIATION REQUIRED
TRAIN overlap is measured but the current private pin lacks verified remediation. This state violates ingestion requirements and requires attention before training selection.
NOT MEASURED
No lexical-decontamination record exists. The source has no cleanliness claim.

The outcome lists below group sources by recorded execution oversight and source status, independently of Quality. A source with FULL content review can still have execution qualification pending. Open a source for its exact pin, counts and evidence.

Recorded execution and source status
CategoryWhat it recordsSources
Grandfathered blendA frozen historical exception; missing environment measurements remain unavailable. It does not establish new QA.
Execution oversight pendingNo qualifying execution oversight is recorded. Inspect content QA separately.
ExcludedAn explicit exclusion with its recorded reason; evidence remains available.
DeprecatedA replacement or withdrawal reason; historical evidence remains available.
Execution oversight SAMPLESome execution checks are sampled. Oracle filtering still covers every eligible task; inspect the receipts for each check.
Execution oversight FULLRecorded execution evidence covers the retained population. This does not certify every grader verdict or establish complete content QA.
SAFE
Measured actor requirements fit the recorded Daytona capability and snapshot rules. Provisioning, quota headroom and completed rollouts are not established.
UNSAFE: reason
Recorded actor requirements exceed a limit or use an unsupported capability. The source remains listed.
N/A or pending
N/A requires a complete census with zero actor machines. Missing measurements remain pending. Grading machines do not enter the actor's Daytona label.

The required ingest order

1 Declare an immutable input

Every source has a registered converter, a canonical ID, an immutable dataset pin and upstream provenance. Historical IDs resolve through the alias table. Register the source through all_sources(); inventory-only declarations are not current runnable sources. See Declarations.

2 Preserve the task contract

New agentic sources ingest TaskCompendium or Harbor task directories. Internal MarinSkyRL format is accepted only for the frozen grandfather list. Prompts, answer contracts, environments and graders belong to the task specification.

3 Assess environment fidelity and grading boundaries

Tasks run in exactly their specified environment. A shared image cannot replace it. A repaired release completely describes its runtime behavior; ingestion-time transformations require SAMPLE or FULL QA and a new pinned version.

Every conversion assesses SHARED versus SEPARATE grading on every task. Workspace state and repository capabilities require SHARED execution; independent submitted-program or typed file-only contracts may use SEPARATE grading. A mismatched boundary is a mechanical rejection. Source-level declarations do not override task requirements. Inspect the per-source census and evidence. See Environments.

4 Convert, deduplicate and decontaminate

The mandatory order is conversion, exact within-source deduplication, lexical decontamination, resource calibration and full-population oracle filtering, then SAMPLE/FULL QA. Raw, unique and dropped counts must reconcile, with a manifest explaining each exclusion.

Lexical measurements bind to the exact dataset revision. TRAIN remediation removes the union of duplicate and lexical exclusions; EVAL sources remove duplicates and retain lexical flags without lexical exclusions. Remediation produces a new private open-athena TaskCompendium release. QA and execution evidence bind to that retained population. Advisory cross-source duplicate groups are distinct from within-source drops and do not authorize deleting data.

QUICK converts without review. SAMPLE uses a bounded QA panel; FULL processes the complete population; complete content review requires its own coverage evidence. Processing mode, execution oversight, content Quality and Result are separate fields. See Within-source deduplication and Lexical decontamination.

5 Filter oracles and qualify execution

Oracle filtering covers every oracle-bearing task in both SAMPLE and FULL. A sampled control pass rate never exempts unsampled oracle-bearing tasks. The retained cohort is the passing subset; infrastructure errors remain errors, with explicit counts and receipts. Content QC remains informational and never rejects tasks.

Sources without oracle solutions

Record payload preservation, execution of the declared setup and verifier liveness separately. A negative verdict requires exit code zero, reward below one and positive structured executed-test evidence; a numeric zero alone does not prove execution. Crashes, timeouts, missing diagnostics and cleanup failures cannot qualify a task. Sampled liveness does not establish full-population execution or solvability.

LLM-judged sources

The implemented JUDGE_TIERS table defines LIGHT, MEDIUM and HEAVY judge specifications. Choose a tier after reviewing ten frozen tasks by hand and record the rationale. Pin the model identity and available revision, rubric, inputs, context and completion budgets, reasoning, temperature, parsing and retry settings. Endpoint configuration stays separate from the task's judge contract.

A pinned preset establishes a contract; source qualification remains pending until end-to-end controls and review demonstrate its behavior through the production grader. Record unavailable immutable weight identities as limitations. The curation reviewer uses its own pinned ReviewerSpec, separate from the task's reward judge. See LLM-judged sources and Oracle filtering.

6 Read actor capacity separately

Daytona labels measure actor machines only. Grading runs according to each task's SHARED/SEPARATE contract and does not change the actor label. A static census does not prove live quota, image availability or successful execution. Per-source backend fit remains unassessed when no current complete task-spec census was loaded.

7 Publish evidence, then load the intended app

Dataset publication, catalog publication, application code release and catalog loading are separate operations. Repaired and converted datasets are private open-athena TaskCompendium releases with immutable pins and provenance. Inspect campaign outcomes before selecting a catalog snapshot. Loading a complete snapshot selects it atomically; failed staging preserves the serving selection.

This preview does not authorize production publication. Follow the Atlas preview procedure with the explicit preview app ID. Production remains on hold.

After admission: training selection

Only TRAIN sources with eligible FULL-mode artifacts may supply a training population. EVAL sources stay evaluation-only. A selection recipe names sources and quotas and pins the heldout set. Its exact heldout matching and cross-source deduplication supplement mandatory version-bound lexical decontamination; they do not replace it or establish semantic decontamination.

Before a training run

  1. Verify the retained dataset pin, intended Use, license and private access.
  2. Read raw/unique/drop counts, lexical remediation and their manifests.
  3. Inspect content Quality, Result and provisional coverage separately from execution qualification.
  4. Check full-population oracle evidence, the SHARED/SEPARATE grading census and backend requirements.
  5. Use the current selection procedure and quick RL loop; Atlas visibility alone does not establish eligibility.

Use or add a source

Read the current catalog

The source table hides QUICK and BAD rows and collapses advisory duplicate groups by default. Show all sources or expand a group to inspect its members. Source evidence links always open the selected source, including entries hidden by table defaults. Missing measurements show as unavailable, never as zero.

Curriculum coverage uses the retained population as primary; the pre-remediation release remains selectable as historical evidence. Coverage applies only to the sources in that release. Approved role corrections show effective Use and preserve sampled evidence's historical role, with a receipt link. Coverage does not establish training eligibility.

Add a source using the maintained procedure

Use Adding a dataset and the task curation reference for current commands, immutable inputs, reviewer configuration and qualification gates. Preserve each attempt's evidence and publish a new version when a task contract changes. A local conversion check does not establish admission or complete QA.

Follow the recorded evidence

Each source page links its pinned current release, upstream input, duplicate/drop manifests, lexical measurements, grading assessment and available QC or execution receipts. Storage pointers include Filer links. Private files require the corresponding Marina or dataset access. A missing field or inaccessible artifact remains an explicit limitation.
